items.text: Once a king thought. <break time="0.8s" /> That he would never fail. <break time="0.8s" /> In anything. <break time="0.8s" /> If he knew three things. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted to know. <break time="0.8s" /> The right time. <break time="0.8s" /> To begin every task. <break time="0.8s" /> And the right people. <break time="0.8s" /> To listen to. <break time="0.8s" /> Above all. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted to know. <break time="0.8s" /> Which work. <break time="0.8s" /> Was the most important of all. <break time="0.8s" /> So he sent a message. <break time="0.8s" /> Throughout his kingdom. <break time="0.8s" /> Promising a great reward. <break time="0.8s" /> To anyone. <break time="0.8s" /> Who could teach him these things. <break time="0.8s" /> Many learned men. <break time="0.8s" /> Came to the king. <break time="0.8s" /> But they all gave. <break time="0.8s" /> Different answers. <break time="0.8s" /> Some said that he should make a careful timetable. <break time="0.8s" /> Of days, months, and years. <break time="0.8s" /> And follow it strictly. <break time="0.8s" /> Others said that he should always pay attention. <break time="0.8s" /> To what was happening. <break time="0.8s" /> And do what was most needed. <break time="0.8s" /> Still others said that he needed a council of wise men. <break time="0.8s" /> And some even said. <break time="0.8s" /> He should ask magicians. <break time="0.8s" /> To the second question. <break time="0.8s" /> Some answered that his advisers were the most important. <break time="0.8s" /> While others named. <break time="0.8s" /> Priests, doctors, or soldiers. <break time="0.8s" /> To the third question. <break time="0.8s" /> Some said science. <break time="0.8s" /> Some said skill in war. <break time="0.8s" /> And others said the worship of God. <break time="0.8s" /> The answers were so different. <break time="0.8s" /> That the king agreed with none of them. <break time="0.8s" /> And gave nobody the reward.

Once a king thought that he would never fail in anything if he knew three things. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted to know the right time to begin every task and the right people to listen to. <break time="0.8s" /> Above all, he wanted to know which work was the most important of all. <break time="0.8s" /> So he sent a message throughout his kingdom, promising a great reward to anyone who could teach him these things. <break time="0.8s" /> Many learned men came to the king, but they all gave different answers. <break time="0.8s" /> Some said that he should make a careful timetable of days, months, and years and follow it strictly. <break time="0.8s" /> Others said that he should always pay attention to what was happening and do what was most needed. <break time="0.8s" /> Still others said that he needed a council of wise men, and some even said he should ask magicians. <break time="0.8s" /> To the second question, some answered that his advisers were the most important, while others named priests, doctors, or soldiers. <break time="0.8s" /> To the third question, some said science, some said skill in war, and others said the worship of God. <break time="0.8s" /> The answers were so different that the king agreed with none of them and gave nobody the reward.

Still wishing to find the answers, the king decided to visit a hermit who was famous for his wisdom. <break time="0.8s" /> The hermit lived in a forest and never left it, and he met only simple, common people. <break time="0.8s" /> So the king put on simple clothes, and leaving his bodyguards behind, he walked to the hut alone. <break time="0.8s" /> When the king arrived, the old hermit was digging the ground in front of his hut. <break time="0.8s" /> He was so weak that he breathed heavily every time he pushed his spade into the earth. <break time="0.8s" /> The king went up to him and said, I have come to you, wise hermit, to ask you three questions. <break time="0.8s" /> The hermit listened to the questions, but he answered nothing and went on digging. <break time="0.8s" /> You are tired, said the king, Let me take the spade and work for a while. <break time="0.8s" /> The hermit gave him the spade and sat down on the ground, and the king dug two beds. <break time="0.8s" /> When the king asked his questions again, the hermit only stood up and held out his hand for the spade. <break time="0.8s" /> But the king did not give it back and kept digging until the sun began to sink behind the trees.

여전히 답을 찾고 싶어서. <break time="0.8s" /> 왕은 한 은자를 찾아가기로 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 지혜로 유명한. <break time="0.8s" /> 은자는 숲에 살았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그곳을 결코 떠나지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그는 오직 만났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 소박하고 평범한 사람들만. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 왕은 수수한 옷을 입었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 호위병들을 뒤에 남겨 둔 채. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 혼자 오두막까지 걸어갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 왕이 도착했을 때. <break time="0.8s" /> 늙은 은자는 땅을 파고 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 자기 오두막 앞에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 너무 약했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 숨을 몰아쉬었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 삽을 밀어 넣을 때마다. <break time="0.8s" /> 땅속으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 왕은 그에게 다가갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 현명한 은자여, 나는 당신에게 왔소. <break time="0.8s" /> 세 가지 질문을 하려고. <break time="0.8s" /> 은자는 질문을 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 아무 대답도 하지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 계속 땅을 팠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 당신은 지쳤소. <break time="0.8s" /> 왕이 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 내가 삽을 잡게 해 주시오. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 잠시 일하게. <break time="0.8s" /> 은자는 그에게 삽을 건넸다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 땅바닥에 앉았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 왕은 밭두둑 두 줄을 팠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 왕이 다시 질문하자. <break time="0.8s" /> 은자는 그저 일어섰다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 손을 내밀었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 삽을 달라고. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 왕은 그것을 돌려주지 않았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 계속 땅을 팠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 해가 지기 시작할 때까지. <break time="0.8s" /> 나무들 뒤로.

Finally the king put down the spade. <break time="0.8s" /> And said. <break time="0.8s" /> I came to you for answers, wise man. <break time="0.8s" /> If you cannot give me any. <break time="0.8s" /> Tell me so. <break time="0.8s" /> And I will go home. <break time="0.8s" /> Someone is running toward us. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the hermit. <break time="0.8s" /> Let us see who it is. <break time="0.8s" /> The king turned and saw. <break time="0.8s" /> A bearded man running out of the woods. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> Against his stomach. <break time="0.8s" /> Blood was flowing. <break time="0.8s" /> From under his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> And when he reached the king. <break time="0.8s" /> He fell to the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> The king and the hermit. <break time="0.8s" /> Opened his clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> And found a deep wound. <break time="0.8s" /> In his stomach. <break time="0.8s" /> The king washed the wound. <break time="0.8s" /> And covered it. <break time="0.8s" /> With his handkerchief. <break time="0.8s" /> And a towel that the hermit had. <break time="0.8s" /> The blood soaked through again and again. <break time="0.8s" /> But the king kept changing the bandage. <break time="0.8s" /> Until it stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> When the man felt a little better. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked for a drink. <break time="0.8s" /> So the king brought him. <break time="0.8s" /> Fresh water. <break time="0.8s" /> By then the sun had set. <break time="0.8s" /> And the air had become cool. <break time="0.8s" /> So they carried the man. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the hut. <break time="0.8s" /> The king was so tired. <break time="0.8s" /> That he lay down on the doorstep. <break time="0.8s" /> And slept through the short summer night.
